stories.headline: Six Winners, Six Median Wins as Week 9 Splits the League Down the Middle
stories.dek: Caleb's Pteem Shteevenshun posted the top score, 138.7, and every head-to-head winner also finished above the 105.1 median.
body: Week 9 drew an unusually clean line through the league. All six head-to-head winners also posted the week's six highest scores, so half the teams went 2-0 and the other half went 0-2. Caleb's Pteem Shteevenshun led the way with 138.7 points, its best total of the season, in a 138.7 to 90.7 win over The House Cats.

Jordan Love carried that game with 36.2 points, the best individual score of the week, and Bijan Robinson added 23.7. Christian McCaffrey scored 21.7 for Luke's side, but the 48.0-point margin was the widest of the week. The result lifted Pteem Shteevenshun from ninth to seventh in the power rankings, the biggest climb of any team.

Tyler's Breece's Pieces beat The Silly Geese 124.2 to 97.3. Joe Burrow started and scored 29.5, with Drake Maye's 18.3 left on the bench, and Ja'Marr Chase added 26.5. Breece's Pieces have now won three straight head-to-head games and cleared the median in each of those weeks. Michael got 28.5 from CeeDee Lamb, while C.J. Stroud scored 35.4 on his bench, the most by any reserve in the league.

Landon's GAYleb williams handled The Mouse Rats 111.4 to 83.5 behind 20.4 points from Javonte Williams. Every Inch Matters beat After Bowers 113.7 to 103.6 as Kenneth Walker III scored 34.3 and Brock Purdy 25.3. Lisan al Gibbs topped I want my Nickleback 113.7 to 79.3, with Christian Watson scoring 26.6; Josh's team finished 0.04 points ahead of Garrett's for the week. Jared's 79.3 was the week's low score.

The upset belonged to Micah. Real Man of Genius beat Illegal use of hands 106.5 to 99.7 and took the sixth and final median spot. After Bowers, at 103.6, missed it by 2.9 points. The median itself has climbed every week since Week 6 and reached 105.1, its highest mark since Week 5.

stories.headline: One Playoff Spot, Six Teams: The Race for Sixth Tightens
stories.dek: After Bowers and The Mouse Rats are tied at 8-10, with Every Inch Matters and Real Man of Genius one game back after two-win weeks.
body: Five weeks and 10 games remain, and the fight for the last playoff spot now runs six teams deep. After Bowers holds the sixth seed at 8-10, level with The Mouse Rats after both went 0-2 in Week 9. Every Inch Matters and Real Man of Genius closed to 7-11 with two-win weeks, and Pteem Shteevenshun and The House Cats sit at 6-12.

Above the line, the top five have some room. Lisan al Gibbs is 16-2, Illegal use of hands 13-5 and The Silly Geese 12-6, while GAYleb williams and Breece's Pieces are both 11-7, three games clear of seventh place. The week also widened the race for the top seed: Josh's lead over Jeremy grew from one game to three.

Ezra's After Bowers has leaned on the median all season. It is 3-6 head-to-head but 5-4 against the median, and its 923.2 points are the most among the six bubble teams except Pteem Shteevenshun. The schedule may help, too. After Bowers' remaining opponents average 98.6 points per game, the second-easiest slate in the league. Every Inch Matters has the hardest, with opponents averaging 109.1.

Pteem Shteevenshun's record hides its scoring. Caleb's team has 960.4 points, fifth-most in the league and more than Breece's Pieces, and its 111.9-point average over the last three weeks ranks fourth. It has also allowed 960.2, almost exactly what it has scored. The House Cats, at 869.3 points, need to make up the same two games.

Week 10 puts two bubble teams head to head. Every Inch Matters hosts Real Man of Genius, with Garrett leading Micah 6-4 all time and projected to win 105.5 to 86.0. After Bowers visits GAYleb williams, which is projected ahead 112.1 to 94.9, though Ezra is 3-1 against Landon. The Mouse Rats visit Breece's Pieces with a 96.1 to 92.7 projected edge, and Bryar is 3-0 against Tyler. Pteem Shteevenshun is projected to beat I want my Nickleback 101.9 to 86.9, and The House Cats visit Illegal use of hands, projected 108.2 to 95.8 against them.

stories.headline: Micah's Season-High 106.5 Ends Jeremy's Six-Game Winning Run
stories.dek: Real Man of Genius beat Illegal use of hands by 6.8 points, handing the league's top-scoring team its first head-to-head loss since Week 2.
body: Real Man of Genius delivered the surprise of Week 9. Micah's team beat Illegal use of hands 106.5 to 99.7, its highest score of the season, and ended Jeremy's run of six straight head-to-head wins. It was only the second time all season that Jeremy's team finished below the median, and the first since Week 2.

Matthew Golden led Micah's lineup with 27.4 points and Tyler Shough added 19.7. The win was the second straight for Real Man of Genius, which beat Pteem Shteevenshun 97.7 to 97.2 in Week 8, the closest game of the season. The 106.5 also earned the team its third median win of the year.

Jeremy got 28.0 from Puka Nacua and 17 from kicker Dominic Zvada, a free-agent pickup on Nov. 4. The bench held more: Tank Dell scored 18.5 there, while Jameson Williams scored 4.5 in the lineup. The 99.7 was Illegal use of hands' lowest total since Week 2 and its first score under 100 since then.

The loss cost Jeremy ground at the top. Illegal use of hands still leads the league with 1,121.7 points, ahead of Lisan al Gibbs at 1,105.0, but it has also allowed 994.0, third-most in the league. Josh's team has allowed 806.4, the fewest. Lisan al Gibbs moved past it to No. 1 in the power rankings, 88.2 to 86.0, and is now three games ahead of 13-5 Illegal use of hands with 10 games left.

For Micah, the win kept Real Man of Genius one game behind sixth at 7-11. Two of its starters arrived in a Week 3 trade with Tyler: Travis Kelce has 40.7 points in five starts and Aaron Jones Sr. 40.1 in four. The next test is a trip to Every Inch Matters, where Garrett leads the series 6-4. Jeremy hosts The House Cats, holding a 3-1 all-time edge over Luke.

stories.headline: Projections Put Three Bottom-Half Teams Above This Week's Median Line
stories.dek: The House Cats, Pteem Shteevenshun and Every Inch Matters are all projected into the top six, with After Bowers and The Silly Geese on the outside.
body: The median game could reshuffle the middle of the standings this weekend. Week 9 projections place The House Cats (120.1), Pteem Shteevenshun (114.7) and Every Inch Matters (114.6), three teams with losing records, among the week's six highest scores, while playoff contenders Breece's Pieces, The Silly Geese and After Bowers sit just below the cut.

Illegal use of hands leads the projections at 123.9, followed by Lisan al Gibbs at 122.6, The House Cats at 120.1 and GAYleb williams at 117.1. The fight for the last two spots could hardly be tighter on paper: Pteem Shteevenshun is projected only 0.04 points ahead of Every Inch Matters. Breece's Pieces is next at 109.1, 5.5 points short of sixth, with I want my Nickleback at 107.0, The Silly Geese at 104.4 and After Bowers at 103.8.

The stakes are highest for Ezra. After Bowers holds the sixth seed at 8-8 with a 3-5 head-to-head record, so its 5-3 mark against the median has done most of the work, and The Mouse Rats are level at 8-8 behind it. Tyler's Breece's Pieces, at 9-7, is 4-4 against the median. Michael's Silly Geese are 6-2 against it but have averaged 98.3 points over the last three weeks, down from 114.9 for the season.

For the teams projected to crash the top six, a median win would be a rare one. Every Inch Matters and Pteem Shteevenshun are each 2-6 against the median, and The House Cats are 3-5. Garrett's team scored 87.5 last week but is projected for 114.6 against After Bowers, which leads that game 10.2 to 0 so far.

The line itself has moved a lot. Weekly medians have ranged from 91.8 in Week 2 to 116.2 in Week 5, and last week's was 100.7. Five teams already have points on the board: Lisan al Gibbs with 20.8, The Mouse Rats with 18.7, The House Cats with 12.0, After Bowers with 10.2 and Illegal use of hands with 8.9. The other seven have yet to score.

stories.headline: Luke and Caleb Meet With a Possible Two-Win Week on the Line
stories.dek: The House Cats lead Pteem Shteevenshun 12.0 to 0, and both teams are projected to finish above the median.
body: The game between The House Cats and Pteem Shteevenshun pairs two teams below .500, but it may carry more weight than any other on the schedule for the winner. Both are projected to clear the median, which means one side could leave the week with two wins. Luke's team leads 12.0 to 0 on the strength of the Jaguars D/ST, and projections favor it 120.1 to 114.7.

The House Cats are 6-10, two games behind After Bowers for the sixth seed with 12 games left, median games included. They have played some of their best football lately, averaging 105.2 points over the last three weeks, third-best in the league behind Illegal use of hands and Lisan al Gibbs. That stretch included wins over I want my Nickleback and The Silly Geese before a 135.5 to 96.2 loss to Lisan al Gibbs last week. Christian McCaffrey leads the roster with 127.0 points in seven starts, and the Jaguars D/ST followed a 21-point Week 8 with 12 more already this week.

Caleb's record undersells his team's scoring. Pteem Shteevenshun is 4-12, yet its 821.7 points rank fifth in the league. It owns the two narrowest losses of the season, 136.9 to 135.5 against Illegal use of hands in Week 3 and 97.7 to 97.2 against Real Man of Genius last week, plus a 3.6-point loss to The Mouse Rats in Week 6. Bijan Robinson (140.8) and Jonathan Taylor (133.7) have been steady all year, and Spencer Shrader, a free pickup, has 67 points in six starts.
Both managers worked the wire this week. Luke claimed J.J. McCarthy for $9 and added Brandon Aiyuk. Caleb picked up Hunter Henry and the Buccaneers D/ST.

The all-time series is even at 2-2. Caleb has reached the playoffs in two of his three past seasons, finishing fourth in 2024 and fifth in 2025. Luke is still looking for his first trip, and a two-win week would pull The House Cats to 8-10 with five weeks to play.

stories.headline: Jared Keeps Reworking His Roster as Lisan al Gibbs Comes to Town
stories.dek: The 2024 champion has made seven trades and spent $95 in FAAB, both league highs, and gets the 14-2 leaders this week.
body: No manager has been busier than Jared. His I want my Nickleback has made seven trades, the most in the league, and spent $95 in FAAB, also the most, while making 33 pickups. The 2024 champion is 3-13 and has lost seven straight, and this week brings the top-seeded Lisan al Gibbs, which leads 20.8 to 0 with Cam Little already scoring 17 points.

Some of the deals have produced. Jayden Daniels, acquired from Garrett in Week 3, has 68.2 points in three starts for Jared, and J.K. Dobbins, part of a Week 5 deal with Michael, has 34.8 in three starts. Jalen Coker, from Ezra in Week 3, has added 22.7. Others have gone the other way: Kenneth Walker III has 75.4 points in four starts for Garrett since leaving in that Week 3 trade, and Alvin Kamara has 35.8 in three starts for After Bowers.

The roster keeps circling back to familiar names. Jared and Garrett traded Kyler Murray and Kendre Miller to each other on Oct. 20, then reversed the swap eight days later. This week, Jared claimed Kyle Pitts Sr. for $5, the tight end he had sent to Ezra in Week 3, and dropped Juwan Johnson, who had arrived in that same deal. He also added Nicholas Singleton, the Bills D/ST and Elijah Mitchell.

The results have yet to follow. I want my Nickleback has scored 720.8 points, second-fewest in the league, and is 1-7 against the median, its lone median win coming in a 129.1-point Week 1. Its last head-to-head win came in Week 5, 82.6 to 55.6 over Real Man of Genius.

Jared does hold a 2-1 all-time edge over Josh, whose team is 14-2 and projected to win 122.6 to 107.0. That projection would leave I want my Nickleback 7.6 points shy of the current median cut, close enough that a strong weekend could snap the losing streak in at least one of its two games.

stories.headline: Two-Time Champion Tyler Gets His Shot at Michael's Silly Geese
stories.dek: Breece's Pieces are projected favorites against the No. 3 seed, though Tyler trails Michael 3-5 in their all-time series.
body: The weekend's marquee game puts the league's only two-time champion against the No. 3 seed. Tyler's Breece's Pieces (9-7) host Michael's Silly Geese (12-4), neither side has scored a point yet, and the projections lean toward the home team, 109.1 to 99.2. It is the first meeting of the season between the two.

History favors Michael, who holds a 5-3 edge in the all-time series. The 2023 season ended with Tyler as champion and Michael as runner-up, and Tyler added a second title in 2025. Michael is still chasing his first; his only playoff trip in three past seasons came in that 2023 run.

Breece's Pieces arrive on a climb. They jumped from ninth to sixth in the power rankings after beating GAYleb williams 118.0 to 103.7 in Week 8, with Ja'Marr Chase scoring 25.6 and Drake Maye 22.5. Bucky Irving leads the roster with 121.6 points in eight starts. The bench has been productive as well: Joe Burrow, acquired from Micah in a Week 3 trade, scored 28.9 in Week 7 and 39.5 in Week 8 without starting.

The Silly Geese have cooled from their early pace. They average 114.9 points a week but 98.3 over the last three, a stretch that included losses to Real Man of Genius and The House Cats before a 111.6 to 87.7 win over I want my Nickleback last week. Josh Allen remains the engine, with 187.3 points in seven starts and 26.6 last week. Michael, who has made five trades and 31 pickups, went back to waivers this week for Devin Singletary, Dylan Sampson, Brian Thomas Jr. and the Bears D/ST.

The stakes run in both directions. The Silly Geese sit four games clear of seventh place with six weeks left, and a win would help them keep pace with the top two seeds. Breece's Pieces are one game above the 8-8 pair of After Bowers and The Mouse Rats, and their remaining opponents average 109.3 points per game, the toughest slate among the league's top eight. Next week brings The Mouse Rats, a team Tyler is 0-3 against all time.

stories.headline: Jeremy Keeps Posting the Week's Top Score, but Josh Still Holds No. 1
stories.dek: Illegal use of hands has led the league in scoring three weeks running and sits one game behind 14-2 Lisan al Gibbs.
body: Jeremy's Illegal use of hands has posted the league's highest score in three consecutive weeks, 148.9, 126.9 and 136.6, and sits first in the power rankings. It still has not caught Lisan al Gibbs. Josh's team is 14-2, one game ahead of Jeremy at 13-3, and both carry early leads into the weekend against teams near the bottom of the standings.

Jeremy has won every head-to-head matchup since Week 3, when he edged Pteem Shteevenshun by 1.5 points. His 1,022.0 points are the most in the league, and his 137.5-point average over the last three weeks is nearly 22 points better than anyone else's. Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 188.0 points as a starter, the top total on any roster, with Kyren Williams at 133.5 and Bhayshul Tuten at 110.8.

The gap comes down to opposing scores. Jeremy has allowed 887.5 points, second-most in the league, while Josh has allowed 727.1, the fewest by almost 50. Lisan al Gibbs has done plenty on its own end, too, with 991.2 points, second only to Jeremy. Its only losses came in Week 4, when GAYleb williams won 126.9 to 97.4 and the score also fell below the median.

Josh has kept building. He traded DK Metcalf and Ollie Gordon II to Jared for Tee Higgins in Week 8, and Higgins scored 32.5 in his first start, the best individual score of the week. Metcalf had produced 60.5 points for Josh before the deal and scored 0.9 in his debut for Jared. Gordon had cost Josh $55 in FAAB in Week 4, still the largest bid of the season. This week Josh claimed Bo Nix for $8.

Both leaders are in good shape for Week 9. Josh leads Jared's I want my Nickleback 20.8 to 0 after Cam Little scored 17.0, and the projection favors him 124.2 to 106.9, though Jared is 2-1 against Josh all time. Jeremy leads Micah's Real Man of Genius 8.9 to 0 on Bhayshul Tuten's early points and is projected to win 124.0 to 91.7. Next week, Josh hosts The Silly Geese while Jeremy hosts The House Cats.

stories.headline: Four Teams Within One Game Fight for the Last Three Playoff Spots
stories.dek: GAYleb williams meets The Mouse Rats, After Bowers visits Every Inch Matters, and The House Cats try to climb back from 6-10.
body: Below the top three, the playoff race is packed tight. GAYleb williams and Breece's Pieces are 9-7, After Bowers and The Mouse Rats are 8-8, and only three of those four can finish in a playoff seed if the standings hold. With six weeks and 12 games left, median games included, Week 9 puts two of them head to head.

Landon's GAYleb williams hosts Bryar's The Mouse Rats in a series tied 2-2 all time. The Mouse Rats lead 18.7 to 0 so far, with Parker Washington scoring 13.1 and Derrick Henry 5.6, but GAYleb williams is projected to win 117.0 to 96.2. Landon's team has the fourth-most points in the league at 877.1 and the softest remaining schedule, with opponents averaging 96.2 points per game.

The Mouse Rats come in after their toughest stretch of the season. They scored 66.7 in Week 8, the lowest total of the week, while Patrick Mahomes put up 25.4 on the bench, and they slid from fifth to eighth in the power rankings. Their 79.4-point average over the last three weeks is the lowest in the league. Bryar was active on the wire, adding Xavier Worthy, Sione Vaki and the Lions D/ST.

Ezra's After Bowers holds the sixth seed largely through the median game. Its head-to-head record is 3-5, but it is 5-3 against the median, and it moved from sixth to fifth in the power rankings. Ezra leads Garrett's Every Inch Matters 10.2 to 0 behind Chris Rodriguez Jr., though the projections favor Every Inch Matters 112.6 to 104.3. Ezra is 4-2 against Garrett all time and has made 42 pickups this season.

The House Cats are two games out of sixth at 6-10, but their 105.2-point average over the last three weeks is the third-best in the league. Luke's team leads Caleb's Pteem Shteevenshun 12.0 to 0 on the Jaguars D/ST and is projected to win 120.0 to 113.5 in a series tied 2-2. Luke added J.J. McCarthy on a $9 claim and Brandon Aiyuk this week, and Rico Dowdle scored 11.6 in his first start after a trade with Jared.
